hints: The required median is the lower middle value in sorted order.
Split the window into a lower half and an upper half using two balanced multisets.
Keep the lower half at size ceil(k/2); its largest element is the median.
analogy: Divide the sorted window at its middle; the rightmost item in the left pile is the answer.
example: For [1,4,2,3] with k=4, the sorted window is [1,2,3,4], so the lower median is 2.
algorithm: Maintain two multisets, with every lower value at most every upper value. Insert and remove the sliding elements, then rebalance so the lower set has ceil(k/2) values in a full window. Output its maximum. Handle duplicates as separate occurrences.
correctness: The order and size invariants place exactly ceil(k/2) values in the lower set, so its maximum is the lower middle element, including for even k.
complexity: For n elements and window size k, O(n log k) time and O(k) space.
